priorities.topic: FOSS offline maps and transit app infrastructure dependency
priorities.angle: CoMaps goes viral (669 HN pts) the same week transit agencies face Google Maps API cost pressure — unpack the dependency chain from transit apps to mapping providers and what the open-source alternative means for urban mobility software
priorities.rationale: CoMaps (FOSS offline maps) hit 669 pts on HN today — the highest transit-adjacent signal. Transit apps like Transit, Citymapper, and Moovit all depend on map tile providers (Google, Mapbox, OSM-derived). StreetComplete also trended (95 pts), reinforcing OSM community momentum. No coverage of open mapping infrastructure in site history. Strong audience overlap with transit/tech readers.

priorities.topic: Edge AI and small language models for transit operations in low-connectivity environments
priorities.angle: Small AI models (7–200 MB) gaining traction in unreliable-network zones maps directly onto transit's hardest infrastructure problem — subway tunnels, rural routes, underground stations. Visual guide to where edge inference is already deployed and what model sizes make it feasible
priorities.rationale: 'Small AI Models Gain Traction in places with unreliable networks' hit 199 pts today. Ternlight (7MB WASM model, 278 pts) adds a parallel data point. Transit systems have always struggled with connectivity gaps in tunnels and rural segments. This is a natural explainer infographic — coverage gap in site history, strong evergreen value.

priorities.topic: AI margin collapse and transit tech vendor pricing risk
priorities.angle: GLM 5.2 analysis of coming AI price compression (567 pts, 349 comments) has direct implications for transit agencies locked into AI vendor contracts — unpack the cost curve, vendor lock-in risk, and what a pricing war means for transit tech procurement cycles
priorities.rationale: Second-highest HN score today. Transit agencies are increasingly committing to AI contracts for demand forecasting, scheduling, passenger analytics. The 'margin collapse' argument is analytically compelling and underreported in transit press. New angle not previously covered on site.

priorities.topic: Gemini Code Assist shutdown July 17 — transit tech team migration guide
priorities.angle: 10 days to deadline. Transit agencies and transit-app developers using Gemini Code Assist need a concrete migration playbook — what to move to, at what cost, by when
priorities.rationale: Genuine timeliness: shutdown is July 17, giving 10 days. This has been queued for several days without being produced. Rank elevated due to shrinking window. Transit tech teams are a core audience subset. Evergreen value drops to zero after July 17.

priorities.topic: Real-time rail network maps — the viral transit data visualization format
priorities.angle: Britain and France real-time rail maps both went viral on HN last week. Why this format resonates, what data it requires, and how US transit agencies compare on public GTFS-RT feed availability
priorities.rationale: Carried over from yesterday's Rank 1 — still fresh (HN story recency), not yet produced, and directly in niche. Good follow-on to prior transit data coverage.
